trust_decision.summary: At every /mockoon-admin/* route the server trusts any HTTP client: no credential is checked, wildcard CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) makes responses browser-readable, GET /mockoon-admin/logs and the SSE stream return transactions containing Authorization/Cookie headers, and POST/PUT/PATCH /mockoon-admin/env-vars writes arbitrary process.env keys. The fix makes the admin API require a per-server bearer token (option, MOCKOON_ADMIN_API_TOKEN or auto-generated), replaces wildcard CORS with a default-deny origin allowlist, redacts sensitive transaction headers before they leave the process, and confines env-var writes to the configured prefix.

landing_point.why: The report names an unauthenticated admin API with wildcard CORS; this middleware owns every /mockoon-admin/* request and the route table below it (admin-api.ts:76-393) is where all admin state is read and written, so an engineer who read only the summary opens this file first.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/serverless/src/libs/serverless.ts:50-59 (serverless wrapper that builds the MockoonServer and drops any token option at the pinned commit; the same wrapper gap exists at packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:266-278 and packages/app/src/main/libs/server-management.ts:70-82)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The admin API lives in @mockoon/commons-server; the serverless package is only a Lambda/Cloud-Functions wrapper with its own enableAdminApi default and the CLI/desktop main process are just option plumbing, so a solver can call the wrapper work 'configuration, not the security fix' and never thread a token into them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The desktop app's Logs tab (and any in-process 'transaction-complete' consumer) must keep receiving full, unredacted request/response headers for the local user; redacting at the shared transaction emitter instead of at each serialization point silently blanks the Authorization/Cookie columns in the UI, and the published fix deliberately redacts only at the admin-API and CLI-log boundaries.

O6_input_shapes: Authorization: Bearer <token> header on normal admin routes vs ?token= query parameter on GET /mockoon-admin/events (EventSource cannot set headers)

one token reused for all environments vs one token per environment vs a comma-separated string in the CLI flag or MOCKOON_ADMIN_API_TOKEN env var (a repeated flag arrives as an array, the env var as a CSV string)
token supplied through options vs MOCKOON_ADMIN_API_TOKEN vs no token at all (auto-generated random hex, per environment, stable across stop/start)
CORS origins absent (default deny), an explicit allowlist (echo origin + Vary: Origin), CSV/repeated flag, and '*' as an explicit wildcard opt-in
env-var key already starting with the configured prefix vs a bare key (auto-prepended) vs an empty prefix (writes rejected but reads still allowed)
header-name case variants over 7 sensitive names, with scheme-preserving redaction for authorization/proxy-authorization (Bearer [REDACTED]) and opaque redaction for cookie/api-key/x-auth-token

O7_producer.where: packages/app/src/main/libs/settings.ts:25-29 (persisted settings loaded from disk; envVarsPrefix and logTransactions reach the admin env-var handlers through packages/app/src/main/libs/server-management.ts:78 and packages/commons-server/src/libs/server/server.ts:295)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Desktop main process forwards every transaction, including raw Authorization/Cookie/X-Api-Key request and response headers, to the renderer over the Electron IPC channel 'APP_SERVER_EVENT' with no redaction
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is local IPC to the app's own renderer, visible only to the machine's user, and the fix itself documents the desktop Logs tab as intentionally unredacted ('NOT applied to: Desktop Logs tab'), so a solver can argue it is outside the admin-API protection.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 3 package boundaries from admin-api.ts (commons-server -> commons -> app main process)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a dockerize entrypoint that forwards --admin-api-token (and --admin-api-cors-origin) into the generated Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dockerize already appends --log-transaction to the entrypoint (dockerize.ts:89-91) and renders it into DOCKER_TEMPLATE (docker.constants.ts:20), so a maintainer shipping admin auth would naturally extend the same flag-forwarding code; a solver who only edits start.ts leaves container builds with no way to pin the token.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second admin-type route group or event stream mounted in createRequestListener outside createAdminEndpoint
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the request listener already mixes admin endpoint creation, databucket generation and global middleware in one place (server.ts:261-323); a maintainer adding a new admin sub-API registers it there, and any per-route or per-handler auth fix misses it while a single app.use prefix covers it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: firebaseApp/netlifyHandler/awsHandler variants that each rebuild the requestListener options
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: three handler flavours already duplicate the requestListener() call, so an option added to one path (or a new handler) can easily be left without the admin token, mirroring the wrapper gap that the published fix had to close.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second localhost HTTP listener with wildcard CORS and no authentication that forwards a ?token= query value to the renderer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the same Electron-main libs family and the same wildcard-CORS pattern as the admin API at the pinned commit, so a maintainer hardening local HTTP surfaces could plausibly add the same origin/token handling here.

O9_family: missing authentication on an administrative interface (CWE-306), with permissive CORS/CSRF as the enabler (CWE-942, CWE-352) and unrestricted environment-variable writes as a privilege/permission issue (CWE-732)

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces (packages/app, cli, cloud, commons, commons-server, serverless); per-package tsc builds (commons-server: tsc -p tsconfig-build.json and tsconfig-build-cjs.json); tests run with node --test via tsx (glob-bin); Node >= 18; node_modules is not present in the pinned tree so an npm install is needed at build time
O10_build.project_tests: packages/commons-server/test/specs/server/admin-api/{data-buckets,env-vars,global-vars,global-state,logs,disable-api}.test.ts (npm test -w @mockoon/commons-server), plus packages/commons-server/test/specs/server/env-vars-prefix.test.ts; CLI test/specs/{run-single-mock,run-multiple-mocks,logging,env-vars-prefix}.test.ts; serverless test/specs/serverless.test.ts; desktop end-to-end specs exist but need Electron and a display.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a token check (and header redaction) inside the GET /mockoon-admin/logs handler only, then validate by calling that one route with and without a Bearer header.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/app/src/main/libs/auth.ts:21-41 runs a separate localhost HTTP listener with wildcard CORS and no authentication that forwards a ?token= query value from the login callback to the renderer; not the admin API sink, not pursued.

Cloud/deployed instances already send 'Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>' to /mockoon-admin (packages/app/src/renderer/app/services/server.service.ts:153, 207-209, 247), and the deploy UI states the instance admin API is always token-protected; that surface is outside the unauthenticated local-server flaw and was not pursued.
